caption: Map range: u from 0..1 into 0.2..0.7, in five steps with an ease - a stepped slice of the palette
why: Remap rescales one range into another; Map range does the same with everything on pins, so a slider or a signal can set the range itself, plus an easing curve and an option to come out in whole steps.
Wire a slider into out high and the person controls the range. Its neighbours: Remap is the quick version with settings; Clamp only cuts; Floor makes steps; Map range does all of it.
steps: **in low** 0 and **in high** 1 is the range it comes from; **out low** 0.2 and **out high** 0.7 is where it goes: only part of the palette is used.
**steps** is 5: the result comes out in five flat steps. **ease** is ease in-out: the steps bunch toward the ends. **clamp** is on: anything outside the in range is held at the ends.
The result is the **Palette**'s index: five bands taking colours from 0.2..0.7 of the palette.

try.label: Smooth
try.text: steps 0: no steps - a smooth sweep through that slice of the palette.

try.label: Whole palette
try.text: out low 0 and out high 1: the full palette across, in five steps.

try.label: Linear
try.text: ease linear: the five steps are evenly spaced.
